After reviewing Sarolta's discovery call and comparing it to your Call 2 framework, this is actually a very strong opportunity. She is absolutely qualified, has a proven track record, already has product-market fit, and isn't looking for "more leads." She's looking for leverage. Your close should revolve around helping her remove herself as the bottleneck while protecting the quality and reputation she has spent 21 years building. fileciteturn0file0L1-L420 fileciteturn0file1L1-L220

# Executive Summary

### Practice Overview
* 21 years in aesthetics specializing in lasers.
* Opened her own practice almost two years ago after leaving an employer where she generated over **$1.4M annually** with outdated technology.
* Beautiful 3,200 sq ft location.
* Premium equipment including Halo, BBL, HydraFacial, Lutronic, Zurf, Bare HR and T Shape 2.
* Three laser providers (including herself) plus part-time injector.
* Around **$32-35k/month** currently with approximately **$12-15k monthly profit.**
* Has never operated in the red.

---

# What She Actually Wants

This is NOT someone chasing marketing.

She wants freedom.

Her goals are:

* Double revenue to $70k+/month
* Remove herself as the only closer
* Build a business that doesn't depend on her physically
* Open multiple locations
* Build a business she can eventually sell
* Finally take a vacation after nearly 30 years

This is the emotional destination.

Not revenue.

Freedom.

---

# Her Biggest Pain Points

## 1. She is the bottleneck.

Everything runs through her.

She does:
* consults
* closing
* training
* operations
* hiring
* patient education

She literally said:

> "I wish I could clone myself."

That should become your headline.

---

## 2. She doesn't trust anyone else to sell.

She likes her staff.

She trusts them.

But...

She knows they cannot convert consultations.

She believes:

"I have to be there."

That means she has created a business...

not a company.

---

## 3. Her body is breaking down.

This is HUGE.

Multiple surgeries.

Hand.

Elbow.

Wrist.

Works 66 hours/week.

She purposely bought lasers easier on her body because she physically couldn't continue.

Tie EVERYTHING back to this.

Because every year she delays...

her body pays for it.

---

## 4. She has invested everything.

Sold her house.

Pulled retirement.

Built her dream clinic.

She isn't protecting money.

She's protecting everything she has built.

---

## 5. She wants predictable scale.

She already has marketing.

She doesn't want another agency.

She specifically rejected agencies who wanted to replace Artemis.

That is massive.

Never position yourself against Artemis.

Position yourselves around it.

Say:

"I actually think Artemis is one of your strengths."

Immediately lower resistance.

---

# Biggest Revenue Leaks

These are exactly how I'd diagnose her.

### Revenue Leak #1

Everything depends on Sarolta.

If she's gone...

consultation conversions fall.

Growth stops.

---

### Revenue Leak #2

No standardized consultation process.

No sales framework.

No scripting.

No provider coaching.

No duplication.

---

### Revenue Leak #3

No scalable patient journey.

Every consultation is different because every provider is different.

---

### Revenue Leak #4

Heavy reliance on individual marketing vendors.

She has:

Laser Hair Company

Artemis

Zurf Agency

Future Agency

Nobody overseeing everything.

No unified patient journey.

---

### Revenue Leak #5

No systematic lifetime value strategy.

She's great at retention...

but admits Halo...

high-ticket lasers...

cross-selling...

reactivation...

could all improve.

---

# How I Would Diagnose Her

I'd say:

> Sarolta, when we first spoke you thought your biggest challenge was marketing and finding someone who could sell the way you do.

> After everything we've discussed today...

> I don't actually think marketing is your biggest problem.

Pause.

> I think marketing is working.

> Artemis is working.

> Laser Hair is working.

> Your referrals are working.

> Your technology is world class.

Pause.

> The real bottleneck...

> is that your business still depends on you.

Everything important still requires Sarolta.

Consultations.

Closing.

Training.

Quality control.

Leadership.

That means the business can only grow as fast as one person.

And unfortunately...

your body has already told you it doesn't want to do this forever.

That is the diagnosis.

---

# Personalize Stage One

Instead of generic wording...

Say:

> Stage One is about identifying exactly where Sarolta exists inside every step of the patient journey.

> Because every place your business depends on you...

is a place your business can't scale without you.

Our first objective isn't getting more patients.

It's making sure the business works without requiring you in every room.

---

# Personalize Stage Two

Do NOT sell leads.

Sell infrastructure.

Say:

> You already have lead sources.

What we're interested in is making every marketing dollar perform better.

That means:

* every inquiry gets followed up
* every consultation follows the same proven framework
* every provider knows how to educate patients the same way you do

Because if we double patient demand tomorrow...

the question isn't whether marketing works.

The question becomes...

can the business deliver the same experience without Sarolta?

---

# Personalize Stage Three

This is where she'll light up.

Say:

> This is probably where I think we create the biggest transformation for you.

You told me several times...

"I wish I could clone myself."

We can't clone you.

But we can absolutely build systems that allow your team to deliver the same patient experience...

the same consultation flow...

the same education...

the same treatment recommendations...

and eventually the same confidence.

Because businesses become sellable...

when excellence becomes systematic...

instead of depending on one extraordinary owner.

---

# Biggest Emotional Future Pace

Don't focus on money.

Say this.

> Imagine it's two years from today.

You own two locations.

Your providers are confidently doing consultations.

Patients receive the same incredible experience whether Sarolta is there or not.

You're finally taking the vacation you haven't had in almost thirty years.

Your phone isn't constantly ringing.

Your team knows exactly what to do.

Your body isn't paying the price for every dollar the business earns.

Would that feel like the business you originally dreamed about building?

That hits every emotional driver she gave you.

---

# Prescription

Priority One

Duplicate Sarolta.

Create consultation systems.

Sales training.

Treatment recommendations.

Closing process.

Provider coaching.

---

Priority Two

Increase lifetime value.

Halo.

BBL.

Zurf.

Memberships.

Reactivation.

Cross-selling.

Referral systems.

---

Priority Three

Build a scalable infrastructure.

Leadership.

Operations.

Marketing integration.

Automation.

So the business becomes sellable.

---

# Objections You'll Probably Hear

### "Marketing is already working."

Agree.

Don't fight it.

Say:

"I actually agree. I don't think marketing is your biggest issue."

---

### "I don't want to replace Artemis."

Perfect.

Say:

"I wouldn't either."

"We're not here to replace what's already working."

"We're here to maximize everything happening after those patients arrive."

---

### "My girls just aren't me."

Exactly.

Say:

"They don't have to become you."

"They need a system that allows them to consistently deliver your standard."

---

# Closing Statement

I'd end with something like this:

> Sarolta, after hearing your story, I don't believe your biggest obstacle is getting more patients.

> I think you've already proven that you know how to attract patients and build trust.

> The challenge is that you've built a practice around one extraordinary provider, and that provider is you.

> You told me you've had multiple surgeries, you work 66 hours a week, you haven't taken a real vacation in almost 30 years, and your dream isn't just to make more money. It's to build a business that can grow without depending on your body.

> That's exactly why I believe we're the right partner.

> Because we're not here to replace the marketing that's already working. We're here to help you build the systems, the team, and the infrastructure that finally allows you to duplicate yourself, increase the value of every patient, and create a business that is scalable, sellable, and gives you the freedom you've earned after 21 years.

> If we can help you build that business, does that feel like the next logical step for where you want to go?

**Coaching for Arlene**

This is an excellent lead and exactly the type of owner we want to work with, but she is **not buying marketing**. She's buying freedom, scalability, and the ability to remove herself as the bottleneck in her business. She already has proven marketing channels that are generating patients, has world-class technology, a strong reputation, and a profitable practice. Her biggest frustrations are that she's the only person who can consistently close consultations, the business still relies heavily on her, and after 21 years in aesthetics her body is paying the price. Don't spend time trying to convince her she needs more leads or that her current marketing is broken, because she'll push back. Instead, validate what's already working, then show her that the real limitation is that the business can't grow beyond Sarolta. Position The Luxora Collective as the partner that will help her duplicate herself through systems, consultation training, team development, retention, and operational infrastructure so she can confidently scale to multiple locations without sacrificing patient experience. If she believes we understand that her goal is to build a business that runs without her instead of simply generating more appointments, you'll have a very high probability of closing this opportunity. fileciteturn0file0L1-L420
